que-es.pregunta: What is OpenMUN and what is it used for?
que-es.respuesta: OpenMUN is an open-source web platform designed to facilitate the moderation and management of Model United Nations (MUN) simulations. It allows Dais Chairs to manage speakers, timers, motions, voting, quorum calculations, and broadcast the live session to delegates and projector screens.

gratuito.pregunta: Is it really 100% free and open source?
gratuito.respuesta: Yes, absolutely. OpenMUN is free software under the GNU AGPLv3 license. It contains no paywalls, premium tiers, or advertisements. All source code is publicly accessible on GitHub to be audited, used, or modified by any committee or institution.

p2p-sync.pregunta: How does live synchronization work (Dais, Delegates, Secretariat)?
p2p-sync.respuesta: OpenMUN uses high-speed encrypted WebSockets and local channels (BroadcastChannel). The Chair acts as the primary room and shares a room PIN or QR code. Timer updates, speakers, and motions are transmitted in real time between devices without storing session data in external databases.

instalacion-cuenta.pregunta: Do I need to install software or create an account?
instalacion-cuenta.respuesta: No. It runs immediately in any modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) across computers, tablets, and smartphones. You can optionally connect Google Drive to sync your files automatically.

persistencia-datos.pregunta: Are my settings saved if I close the browser?
persistencia-datos.respuesta: Yes. All session progress (speakers, voting, quorum, and notes) is automatically saved locally in your browser (LocalStorage). You can also export and import your full configuration via JSON or Excel, or sync with Google Drive.

importar-paises.pregunta: How can I import my country or delegation roster?
importar-paises.respuesta: In the 'Setup' tab or via the 'Import Countries' widget, you can upload Excel spreadsheets (.xlsx/.xls) or paste a plain text list. The system automatically creates the country matrix and calculates quorum. Banners, emojis, or SVGs are automatically matched for current countries.

modo-offline.pregunta: Can I use OpenMUN without an internet connection (offline)?
modo-offline.respuesta: Yes. Once the page is loaded, all Chair tools (timers, GSL, motions, voting) work 100% offline. To project on a second screen offline, you can open the Secretariat view in an additional window. You will lose the ability to connect with Backroom and delegations, as well as synchronization with conferences.

como-funcionan-conferencias.respuesta: When you create a conference, we save a file in our database. When you join it, you modify or read that file. The database is private and no one other than you and us has access. Since this space is limited, announcements are deleted after 24 hours and entire conferences after one month *without activity in the conference*. If you provide an email address, we will send you a file containing all conference information so you don't lose anything.

donar.pregunta: How is OpenMUN funded and maintained?
donar.respuesta: For you, OpenMUN is free. For us, building and hosting it requires time, effort, and money. We keep it free so anyone can use it, while relying on donations from those who can support our work.

colaborar.pregunta: How can I contribute, suggest improvements, or report bugs?
colaborar.respuesta: You can open an issue or Pull Request on our GitHub repository, or write directly to contacto@openmun.app. Every contribution and suggestion is warmly welcomed.

liveSession.donateParagraph3: Real-time synchronization features between chairs, delegates, and backroom cost us real infrastructure money each month. We want to keep this open for everyone, but we rely on those who can contribute to help cover hosting expenses.
liveSession.donateParagraph4: If you use these live server features, donating about €5 per 50 delegates (or per committee) covers costs and makes us very happy.
liveSession.donateParagraph5: If you can give more, fantastic! And if you cannot donate anything, do not worry at all! Enjoy the tool, get the most out of it, and help us by spreading the word about OpenMUN.

legalBanner.title: Privacy & Transparency Notice
legalBanner.description: At OpenMUN we prioritize your privacy: this website DOES NOT use tracking or third-party cookies. We only store your Model UN session locally on your own browser (LocalStorage).

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: OpenMUN has been designed from its origin under the principle of Privacy by Design and by Default. Our commitment is absolute transparency and minimum data processing strictly necessary for the platform to operate.
privacy.noCookiesTitle: Free of Advertising & Tracking Cookies Guarantee
privacy.noCookiesHeading: We Do NOT Use Advertising or Tracking Cookies
privacy.noCookiesDescription: At OpenMUN we do NOT use tracking cookies, third-party cookies, or advertising pixels. We do not build user profiles or monetize your information under any circumstances.
privacy.sec1Intro: OpenMUN operates through two modes depending on the feature you use:
privacy.sec1LocalDesc: If you run a standard committee without central synchronization, data (committee names, delegate rosters, motions, timers, and interface preferences) is stored exclusively locally in your browser via LocalStorage. This data is never sent to our servers and can be deleted by clearing your browser storage.
privacy.sec1ConfDesc: If you create or manage a synchronized conference with multiple committees, conference structure, debate states, and participant rosters are processed and stored in a secure database on our server to enable real-time synchronization and active room persistence.
privacy.sec2Intro: If you voluntarily choose to provide your email address to receive a backup file of your conference:
privacy.sec2Finalidad: Purpose: We will use your email exclusively to send you the exported file of your conference or committee.
privacy.sec2BaseJuridica: Legal basis: Explicit consent when requesting the dispatch of said file.
privacy.sec2Conservacion: Retention: Your email address is used temporarily to process delivery and is not used for marketing purposes, newsletters, or shared with third parties.
privacy.sec2Terceros: Third-party providers: For email delivery, we may rely on transactional email infrastructure services complying with European data protection regulations.
privacy.sec3Desc: Live synchronization features (such as Delegate, Secretariat, or Backroom mode) use secure WebSockets (wss://). Debate event communication is transmitted encrypted in transit between connected clients and the sync server.
privacy.sec4Desc: If you voluntarily link your Google Drive account for personal backups, authorization tokens are securely stored in your browser. Backups transfer directly between your browser and your personal Google Drive storage, without server intermediation.
privacy.sec5Desc: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics solely to monitor technical performance and overall platform traffic volume. This tool uses no cookies, stores no persistent identifiers, and does not track individual navigation across different websites.
privacy.sec6Desc: You have the right to access, rectify, restrict, or request the deletion of data stored on our servers (including conference removal or email log deletion). To exercise these rights, contact us at contacto@openmun.app.
privacy.sec7Desc: OpenMUN is an independent Free Software project. Anyone can audit the public source code on our GitHub repository to verify technical operation and strict respect for privacy.
privacy.sec8Desc: If you have questions regarding this policy or the technical handling of data, reach us at contacto@openmun.app.

terms.pageTitle: OpenMUN - Terms and Conditions of Use
terms.title: Terms and Conditions of Use
terms.subtitle: Welcome to OpenMUN, a free and open web platform designed to optimize management and debate in Model United Nations.
terms.sec1Desc: OpenMUN is offered freely and without cost for conferences, educational institutions, dais chairs, and delegates. Its main objective is to enrich academic culture, constructive debate, and school/university diplomacy.
terms.sec2Desc: OpenMUN is a project originally developed by Lucas R. Kowalski and distributed as Free Software. You are completely free to use, modify, and share it, always respecting author moral rights and the open source license terms available in its official GitHub repository.
terms.sec3LocalDesc: The user is solely responsible for custody of data held in LocalStorage or in their personal Google Drive account. Clearing browser cache or data will delete sessions not previously exported.
terms.sec3ConfDesc: In conferences synchronized through the server, OpenMUN facilitates concurrency between committees and provides export mechanisms (including sending the file via email). Nonetheless, OpenMUN is a live debate support tool and does not constitute an indefinite cloud storage service; exporting the session file (.json) at the end of each session or debate is strongly recommended.
terms.sec4Desc: The user agrees not to use server infrastructure, WebSockets, or the conference database to execute denial of service attacks, unauthorized flood requests, malicious code injection, or any unlawful activity that harms service availability for other committees.
terms.sec5Desc: The software is provided "AS IS", without warranties of any kind regarding uninterrupted availability, error-free operation, or fitness for a particular purpose. OpenMUN is not liable for potential data loss caused by local network failures, user connectivity issues, or third-party infrastructure outages.
terms.sec6Desc: We reserve the right to update these terms to reflect technical improvements or regulatory changes. The current version will always remain publicly accessible on the platform.
terms.sec7Desc: To resolve doubts or inquiries related to these conditions, you can email contacto@openmun.app.
